candor

/KAN-der/ - the stress falls on KAN · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Candor means openness and honesty in speech.

The chef answered the health inspector with unexpected candor, pointing out two violations the inspection itself had missed.

Example

When the museum unveiled its restoration, the head conservator spoke with disarming candor: two of the panel's blues were modern guesses, she said, and pointed to exactly where.

Candor goes past ordinary honesty. Honesty answers truthfully when asked; candor volunteers the uncomfortable part unasked, in plain words, with nothing softened for the listener's comfort.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

frankness: Frankness is plain, unguarded speech — saying what you actually think, with a hint of bluntness about it. Candor shares that plainness but adds the volunteering: candor offers the uncomfortable truth before anyone asks for it, while frankness only promises directness once a person has decided to speak.

openness: Openness is a general willingness to share — information, feelings, plans — in speech or in manner. Candor is narrower and costlier: candor volunteers the damaging detail in plain words, unasked. An open person shares readily on most things; candor means honesty precisely where sharing hurts.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

evasiveness: slides around the question without ever answering it

double-talk: language built to sound like an answer while hiding one

Where it sits · how freely hard truths are offered

tact → honesty → candor

tact vs. candor: Tact is the gentlest rung, far milder than candor — tact trims and times the truth to spare feelings, telling only as much as the moment can bear.

honesty vs. candor: Honesty stops short of candor: honesty answers truthfully when asked, while candor volunteers the uncomfortable truth before anyone asks.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cand-: to shine, to glow white (Latin candere)

Suffix — -or: state or quality

Put it together: Latin candere meant 'to shine, to glow white,' and candor was whiteness itself — the quality of a surface with nothing painted over it. English kept the picture: speech with candor is white light, unshaded and untinted. The same glow burns in candle and incandescent — and in candidate, from Rome's office-seekers in their specially whitened togas.

Use the root in a new word: candidate: Both candidates for club treasurer promised to open the books by Friday.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / admiring

Candor is the noun for openness that costs something — reports, testimony, hard conversations — and it usually carries admiration. Forthright, taught in this same unit, is its adjective-side twin for describing people and answers; where the plainness starts to bruise, English reaches for bluntness instead.
